age.evidence: weighed between 35 and 55 g and were 3 -4 months in age

sex.evidence: Male Swiss-Webster mice (CFW: Charles River Laboratories, INC Wilmington, MA) served as the subjects in all experiments

dosing.evidence: varying doses of DOI (0.1 0.32, 1, 3.2, and 10 mg/kg); All compounds were dissolved in sterile saline and delivered through intraperitoneal injection
evaluate the effects of fluoxetine on psilocybin-induced HTR (0.32, 1, 1.8, 3.2, and 10 mg/kg)

dosing.doses_raw: 10 or 32 mg/kg (acute); 10 mg/kg daily for 14 days (chronic)
dosing.evidence: animals received a single injection of either fluoxetine (10 or 32 mg/kg)... animals were administered daily injections of either saline or 10 mg/kg fluoxetine [for 14 days]

group_housing.evidence: All mice were housed in groups of 5

day_night_flipped.evidence: Mice were housed in rooms maintained on a 12 h light/dark cycle. The lights were turned off at 7 p.m. and turned back on at 7 a.m. every day. All experiments were conducted during the light phase.

assays.assay_description: Mice injected i.p. with R(-)DOI or psilocybin (with prior saline or fluoxetine pretreatment, acute or chronic 14-day) and placed individually in acrylic chambers. HTR scored offline from video by two trained observers starting 10 min post-injection for 10 min. Includes acute fluoxetine + DOI, chronic fluoxetine + DOI, 14-day fluoxetine discontinuation + DOI, and acute fluoxetine + psilocybin variants.

application_type.evidence: All compounds were dissolved in sterile saline and delivered through intraperitoneal injection

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were set in a room to acclimate for 30 min (room acclimation only; no apparatus habituation described)

setup_restrain.evidence: placed individually into acrylic chambers, where a video recording system was set up above

food_restriction.evidence: Mice had access to food (Laboratory Rodent Diet) and water ad libitum [in home cage]; testing occurred in acrylic chambers

water_restriction.evidence: Mice had access to food... and water ad libitum [in home cage]; testing occurred in acrylic chambers

time_to_assay.evidence: HTR behavior in each subject was recorded 10 min postinjection of each psychedelic

outcomes.summary: Acute high-dose fluoxetine (32 mg/kg) shifted the DOI HTR dose-response curve rightward (~10-fold reduced potency), while acute 10 mg/kg fluoxetine had no effect on DOI. Chronic fluoxetine (10 mg/kg, 14 days) reduced DOI Emax without altering potency; this attenuation was reversed after a 14-day washout. Acute 10 mg/kg fluoxetine attenuated the efficacy (Emax) but not potency of psilocybin-induced HTR.
outcomes.evidence: acute fluoxetine pretreatment attenuates DOI-induced behavior in a dose-dependent manner... chronic fluoxetine decreases the efficacy but not the potency of DOI-induced HTR... attenuation... fully recovered after washout... acute fluoxetine attenuates the maximal behavioral response to psilocybin without altering its potency

B1_num_measures.evidence: HTR counts (Mean ± SEM) — single behavioural measure

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: recorded for a duration of 10 min; total HTR counts reported, no within-session time-course

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B6_cognitive.evidence: drug-elicited HTR is a reflexive 5-HT2A readout, no learning required

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each session was scored by two trained observers

B8_multivariate.evidence: nonlinear regression on a single measure; no PCA/UMAP/clustering

E2_shelter.evidence: acrylic chambers with video recording from above; no shelter described

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/water in the testing chamber

D1_continuity.evidence: For chronic and discontinuation doses, mice were tested twice (once at the end of chronic dosing and again at the end of the discontinuation phase)

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded for a duration of 10 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Chronic and discontinuation cohorts had HTR recorded on 2 days (day 14 of dosing and day 28 after washout)

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug HTR baseline recording reported

D5_followup.evidence: mice stopped receiving fluoxetine for the next 14 days, following which HTR was evaluated again across a range of DOI doses

judge_notes: Both candidates identified a single HTR assay; merged into one entry that spans all variants (acute fluoxetine + DOI, chronic fluoxetine + DOI, 14-day discontinuation + DOI, acute fluoxetine + psilocybin) per rubric rule that dose/schedule variants of the same paradigm = 1 assay.
B1: HTR is a single behavioural measure (head twitch count) → score 0 (qwen correct; overrode glm).

D1/D3/D5: chronic and discontinuation cohorts were tested on 2 separate days (end of chronic dosing and end of washout) per Methods, so D1=Multiple sessions, D3=2-7, D5=Yes (qwen correct; overrode glm).
setup_habituation: paper describes only room acclimation, not apparatus habituation, so scored 'no' rather than 'yes' (overrode glm).
qPCR, brain dissection are non-behavioural and excluded per rubric.
